name: How are heating and cooling handled for an added second story?

mainEntity.name: How are heating and cooling handled for an added second story?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heating and cooling an added upper floor usually requires a dedicated system rather than connecting to your existing furnace and air conditioner. Upper levels absorb significant heat through the roof, making temperature control difficult if tied to a single ground-level thermostat. Contractors generally recommend installing either a separate secondary HVAC unit with its own ductwork or multi-zone ductless mini-split heat pumps. Evaluating your electrical panel capacity is an important early step, as adding new climate control systems often requires a panel upgrade.
acceptedAnswer.description: Upper floors usually require a dedicated HVAC system or ductless mini-split units, as existing ground-floor furnaces rarely have the capacity to heat and cool both levels.
